title: Leak changes the strongest recipient in passive models of two partial adult worm electrical maps
abstract: We tested whether membrane leak changes the strongest steady voltage recipient in passive models of two adult C. elegans electrical maps. We treated junction counts as symmetric conductance weights and scaled each map to mean weighted degree one. Changing uniform leak from 0.01 to 1 changed the strongest remote recipient for 42 of 145 sources in map 7 and 23 of 147 in map 8. For 37 and 20 sources, each endpoint winner exceeded the other by more than 1 percent. Across 131 common sources, the two maps shared a winner for 57 sources at leak 0.01 and 54 at leak 1. A maximum-principle argument shows that a strongest remote recipient must be a direct neighbor in this model. A five-cell example shows why the largest direct weight need not win at small leak. Partial annotations, assumed conductances and leak values, and the absence of active and chemical signaling prevent a claim about measured responses. The package includes graph arrays, full transfer matrices, source checks, code, and a static figure.

display.caption: Leak changes recipient order in two passive electrical models. The left panel compares each sampled leak with 0.001. The middle panel permits ties in direct counts. The right panel compares the two full models on 131 common source and recipient labels. These are model calculations, not measured responses.
